v.why: Benchmark results show a dead edge is far more costly than a weak one, so filling an empty edge with a 3x3 conv gains much more than upgrading an existing op.
Adding a direct input-to-output residual path helps much more than swapping a conv for a skip, which usually loses accuracy.
Gains from extra convs diminish once a direct skip path already eases optimization.
Pooling is a weak op, so replacing a 3x3 conv with it costs much more accuracy than replacing a skip or none.
Extra convolutions show diminishing returns when a strong 3x3 conv already sits early in the cell.
Replacing a weak pooling op with a skip helps, whereas replacing a conv with a skip hurts.
Filling the final edge into the output with any conv recovers far more accuracy than swapping between non-empty ops.
A skip on the direct edge is already a strong component, so a conv replacing it gains little compared with filling a none edge.
Component value depends on what else is present: a second 3x3 conv adds less when another 3x3 conv already feeds the output.
Even a weak pooling op beats an empty edge, but replacing a conv with pooling loses accuracy.
